overview: Congress previously authorized a memorial in Washington, D.C., honoring Thomas Paine, the Revolutionary-era writer of the pamphlet "Common Sense." This bill would approve placing that memorial in Area I, the central part of the capital around the National Mall that is reserved for memorials of the greatest historical importance. It sets aside the usual requirements of the Commemorative Works Act, the law that governs how memorials in the capital are approved and where they go, and requires the Paine memorial to be built within Area I. As of October 29, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say Paine's writing helped inspire American independence, and that a place near the nation's most important monuments fits his role, especially around the country's 250th anniversary.
against: Critics say the bill skips the usual review process for siting memorials on the limited space of the National Mall area, which could set a precedent for other memorials to bypass it too.
